title: Comparing Very Large and Small Numbers
short: Compare and estimate with powers of 10.

blocks.html: Scientific notation makes it quick to compare very large and very small numbers, because the exponent tells you the size at a glance.

Every first factor is at least 1 and less than 10. So any number with $10^{6}$ is between one million and ten million, and any number with $10^{7}$ is at least ten million. No first factor can make up a whole power of 10, so the exponent decides first.

To compare two positive numbers in scientific notation, compare the exponents first; the larger exponent wins. Only when the exponents match do you compare the first factors. To find how many times as large one number is, divide.

blocks.cap: On the lower line, each step to the right multiplies by 10, so every power of 10 gets the same space. Move the point and compare where it sits on the two lines.

blocks.title: Exponents first
steps: Compare the exponents: 6 is greater than 5.

blocks.title: Negative exponents
steps: $-4$ is greater than $-5$ (it is closer to 0).

blocks.title: How many times as large?
blocks.q: The United States has about $3 \times 10^{8}$ people. The whole world has about $8 \times 10^{9}$. About how many times as many people live in the world?
steps: With these rounded values, about 27 times as many.

blocks.title: Estimate with one digit
blocks.q: Estimate $4{,}870{,}000$ as a single digit times a power of 10.
steps: Round 4.87 to the nearest whole number: 5.

blocks.html: Comparing the first factors before the exponents, and deciding that $9 \times 10^{3}$ is greater than $2 \times 10^{5}$ because 9 is greater than 2. Write them out to check: 9,000 and 200,000.
